clue.text: Bearer of wine giving a service in church

indicators.note: in places the article and the service inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a church service offers in the way of communion wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass jug used for serving wine at table is a container that carries it.

clue.text: 6 showing yellow wee

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, as does chicken
wee is Scots for small

explanation.surface: A cartoon showing a timid small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is ANIMATION: the answer is an animated Disney film about a nervous young bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2005 Disney film is an example of animation, the subject of 6 down.

clue.text: See 14
Queen in decline without a cleaner

indicators.note: in puts the queen's name inside what is left of the word for decline
without says the letter A is taken away from the word for decline

parts.note: a decline is a fall
Queen Anne, British monarch 1702-14

explanation.surface: A monarch in reduced circumstances must do without a char.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the A, leaving FLL for 'in' to wrap round the queen. In Britain a flannel is a small face cloth, hence a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a small towelling cloth for washing the face is a cleaning item.

clue.text: In the interests of man to cut fat back?

indicators.note: back says the whole assembly is read from end to start
to cut means the man's pronoun slices into the word for fat

parts.note: flab is body fat
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Is it for the man's own good to trim his paunch?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' and 'back' work on the whole: the result is FLAHEB turned round. The definition stands for the word as used in 'on behalf of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on someone's behalf means acting for their benefit, in their interests.

clue.text: Raise some genial, educated girl

indicators.note: Raise says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Bring up a pleasant, well-schooled young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Raise' tells you to read upwards: ENIALE runs across 'genial, educated', and backwards it gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, as crosswords often use girl for any female first name.

clue.text: Paul's in a state — that's life!

indicators.note: in places the setter's contraction inside the word for state

parts.note: a nation is a state
Paul is the setter, so Paul's means 'I am', shortened to I'M

explanation.surface: The setter declares himself in a fine fettle and calls it living.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is this puzzle's setter, so 'Paul's' is the setter saying I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation is liveliness, vitality: being full of life.

clue.text: 6 where wild dog gobbles pieces up after bit of fish

indicators.note: after puts the dog and its meal behind the bit of fish

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish

indicators.note: gobbles means the dog swallows the pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: the dingo is Australia's wild dog

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: men are pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A cartoon in which a feral hound wolfs down scraps after a fish part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the pieces upwards in this down clue, and 'gobbles' makes DINGNEMO; 'after' sets it behind the fin. 6 is ANIMATION: this is Pixar's film about a lost clownfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The 2003 Pixar film is an example of animation, the subject of 6 down.

clue.text: Useless oaf Clinton cavorting with nun

indicators.note: cavorting is leaping about wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A clumsy former president frolics with a nun, to no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' rearranges OAF CLINTON NUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nonfunctional does not work, so it serves no purpose.

clue.text: Round sound?

definitions.meaning: to make a bell chime, or a telephone call

explanation.definitionFit: A circle is a ring, and to ring is to make a bell or phone sound.

clue.text: Lesser jobs returning Mexican food in French planes

indicators.note: in places the turned-round food inside the French word

parts.note: avions is French for aeroplanes

indicators.note: returning says the food's letters go back the other way

parts.note: a taco is a Mexican filled tortilla

explanation.surface: Minor work involves bringing tortillas back on French aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the food to OCAT. Avocations are minor occupations or hobbies, not a word for holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocations are hobbies or sideline occupations, secondary to one's main work.

clue.text: Sport screened by covering feature in Chamonix, for example

indicators.note: screened by means hidden behind, so the sport sits inside the covering

parts.note: skin is a covering
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A game shown on TV under cover in a French Alpine resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Chamonix is a ski resort in the French Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski slopes are a standard feature of an Alpine resort such as Chamonix.

clue.text: Loud 6, not the first as 6

parts.note: f, forte, means loud in music

indicators.note: not the first says the earlier of two occurrences of the letters is removed

parts.note: 6 is the animation entry, and Anastasia is a 1997 animated film

explanation.surface: A noisy cartoon, unlike the first one, counted as a cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first as' means the 1997 film's title loses the earlier of its two AS runs, leaving ANTASIA. The second 6 is the definition: Disney's 1940 film.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's 1940 film set to classical music is a landmark of animation.

clue.text: Elitist admitting western soprano dazzled

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the snob takes the abbreviation inside

parts.note: a snob is an elitist
Jenny Lind was a famous Swedish soprano, the 'Swedish Nightingale'

explanation.surface: A snooty person lets in a cowboy singer who is blinded by the lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' puts W inside SNOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow-blindness is sight lost to glare from snow, so being dazzled by brightness.

clue.text: Partial 6 doctor put in the picture, OK to go on

parts.note: Doctor Who is the BBC's time-travelling hero
framed means set in a picture frame, or wrongly incriminated
roger is radio-speak for OK, message received
to rabbit, or rabbit on, is British slang for to chatter at length

explanation.surface: A doctor briefed on a case gets the go-ahead to keep talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1988 film mixes live action with cartoons, so it is only partly animation (6).
explanation.definitionFit: The film combines real actors with cartoon characters, so it is partly an animated film.

clue.text: See 16 down
Communist movement?

definitions.meaning: a Trotskyist, a follower of Trotsky
a horse's gait between walk and canter

explanation.definitionFit: Trot is short for a Trotskyist, and also names a horse's pace.

clue.text: 6 like nothing else

indicators.note: else means otherwise, in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An animated film unlike anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'else' rearranges LIKE NOTHING. 6 is ANIMATION: this is Disney's 1994 film.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's 1994 film about a young lion is an example of animation.

clue.text: Get seaman ordered for Boy George, perhaps

indicators.note: ordered means put in a fresh sequence, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fetch a sailor that a pop singer asked for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges GET SEAMAN. Boy George is the professional name of singer George O'Dowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Boy George is the performing name of George O'Dowd, an example of a pseudonym.

clue.text: Party laid on for knight

parts.note: a gala is a festive party
had in the sense of laid on or held, as an event

explanation.surface: A celebration was staged for a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Galahad was the purest of King Arthur's knights.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad was a knight of the Round Table in Arthurian legend.

clue.text: He has the bottle to exploit isle

parts.note: to milk is to exploit
the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Someone brave enough to take advantage of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain milk was delivered in glass bottles to the doorstep by a milkman.
explanation.definitionFit: The man delivering milk carries bottles; 'bottle' is also slang for courage.

clue.text: See 14
Why attention given to pudding in the distant past

parts.note: Y sounds like the word why
to give ear is to pay attention
sago is a milky pudding

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why a dessert got so much notice long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Long ago, a phrase for a time far back in history.

clue.text: See 1 down
In which beer is capital

parts.note: a tun is a large cask, a vessel in which beer is held

explanation.surface: A town where ale is the chief thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'In which beer is' as TUN, the barrel beer is in, followed by IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia.

clue.text: McDonald's given foot, one gathered, on every strip in Florida

parts.note: the golden-arches logo of McDonald's is the letter M

indicators.note: gathered means the metrical foot collects the numeral inside it

parts.note: an iamb is a metrical foot
I is the Roman numeral one
each means every

explanation.surface: A burger chain's beach outlet, with poetic feet and everyone in Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' puts I inside IAMB to give IAMIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami Beach is a narrow barrier island city along the Florida coast.

clue.text: See 7
Having backed horse, shame non-starter given total exposure

indicators.note: backed says the horse's letters run back to front

parts.note: a dun is a greyish-brown horse

indicators.note: non-starter means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a pity is a shame

explanation.surface: After betting on a horse, it is a shame the outsider failed to run in full view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns DUN into NUD; 'non-starter' takes P off PITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudity is being naked, completely exposed.

clue.text: My boss is working to become an inventor

parts.note: a newspaper setter's boss is the editor, ED
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A setter's editor is busy trying to become an innovator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My boss' is the setter's editor; MY BOSS is not an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and practical light bulb.
